AL.name: Alabama

severance.text: Alabama's rule (Ala. Admin. Code r. 480-4-3-.33) says wages in lieu of notice and dismissal or separation allowances affect eligibility only if all three conditions hold: the payment is legally enforceable, the agreement names the period after termination it covers, and some continuing employer-employee tie exists. Severance paid without regard to the employee's status after termination does not affect eligibility.

payInLieuOfNotice.text: The same Alabama rule (Ala. Admin. Code r. 480-4-3-.33) covers wages in lieu of notice. They affect eligibility only if the payment is legally enforceable, the agreement names the period after termination it covers, and some continuing employer-employee tie exists.

workSearch.text: DOL Table 5-14 (2023 Comparison): claimants must complete at least 3 work search activities per week.

AL.notes: State not listed in DOL Table 5-18; both values are filled from the state administrative code. The rule says these payments 'affect eligibility' but does not say whether they reduce benefits or deny them for the week. The claimant handbook does not address severance. DOL values reflect state law as of 2023-01-01 (2023 Comparison, the latest edition published); verify against the state agency before relying on them.

The DLT FAQ says you are eligible for a partial payment if your weekly severance is less than your benefit rate (https://dlt.ri.gov/individuals/unemployment-insurance/unemployment-insurance-faq). No official source addresses pay in lieu of notice. DOL values reflect state law as of 2023-01-01 (2023 Comparison, the latest edition published); verify against the state agency before relying on them.

SC.name: South Carolina

severance.text: South Carolina DEW's claimant handbook (as of 9/3/2025) says the agency may contact you for details to determine whether your separation pay is deductible.

workSearch.text: DOL Table 5-14 (2023 Comparison): claimants must complete at least 2 work search activities per week. Limitations or specific requirements apply. Registering with employment services, using reemployment services, attending a job-seeking workshop, or taking part in job search activities may count. South Carolina requires 2 contacts through the state system.

WA.name: Washington

severance.text: Washington ESD says severance pay does not usually affect benefits, as long as it is not assigned to a period after separation, you are not on call, benefits do not keep accruing, and a new job does not affect the severance. RCW 50.04.320(4)(b) excludes severance pay from assigned remuneration.

payInLieuOfNotice.text: DOL Table 5-18 (2023 Comparison): the weekly benefit is reduced by the weekly prorated amount of the payment.

workSearch.text: DOL Table 5-14 (2023 Comparison): claimants must complete at least 3 work search activities per week. Registering with employment services, using reemployment services, attending a job-seeking workshop, or taking part in job search activities may count.

WA.notes: DOL Table 5-18 cell for dismissal/severance payments is blank. DOL Table 5-18 dismissal-payment cell reads 'P' with footnote 6: 'Previously accrued compensation except severance pay, when assigned to a period of time by collective bargaining or trade practices; negotiated settlements or proceeds given for early termination of an employment contract.' The footnote appears to exclude severance pay itself, so severance treatment is not confirmed from DOL. Severance is resolved from ESD and RCW 50.04.320 (https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=50.04.320). ESD says to report pay in lieu of notice but does not state its effect; the DOL 'reduces' entry is kept. DOL values reflect state law as of 2023-01-01 (2023 Comparison, the latest edition published); verify against the state agency before relying on them.

severance.text: WorkForce West Virginia's claimant handbook says severance pay or severance packages are not deductible income and do not affect the weekly benefit amount.

workSearch.text: DOL Table 5-14 (2023 Comparison): claimants must actively seek work each week; the minimum number of weekly work search activities is listed as "Unspecified". The number depends on geography, labor market, union hall membership, or other factors.

Code 21A-6-3(5)(a) disqualify a claimant for a week of wages in lieu of notice, but the claimant handbook says wages in lieu of notice are deductible income that does not affect the WBA. WI.name: Wisconsin

severance.text: DOL Table 5-18 (2023 Comparison): the weekly benefit is reduced by the weekly prorated amount of the payment. This applies only when the payment is allocated by the close of the week, payable at the full applicable wage rate, and the claimant had notice of the allocation. A claimant is ineligible for any week with 32+ hours of termination pay totaling over $500, alone or combined with wages.

workSearch.text: DOL Table 5-14 (2023 Comparison): claimants must complete at least 4 work search activities per week. The agency may increase or direct the requirement.

WI.notes: DOL Table 5-18 cell for wages in lieu of notice is blank. Wis. Stat. 108.05(5) and 108.05(3) confirm the DOL severance entry. The DWD handbook lists pay in lieu of notice as reportable and says only that it 'may affect your UI' (https://dwd.wisconsin.gov/uiben/handbook/maintaining.htm), so it stays null. DOL values reflect state law as of 2023-01-01 (2023 Comparison, the latest edition published); verify against the state agency before relying on them.
